forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.role_in_assembly: Rewrites the reduced Gaussian quotient as the shifted product P_{a,b,r}(q).

domain_restrictions: r = n - a - b, so r is a nonnegative integer
The q-binomial definition uses nonnegative integer inputs for the q-Pochhammer factors
The ratio is only meaningful when the denominator is nonzero, unless the identity is interpreted formally
The product from i = a + 1 to b is an empty product when a = b, and then it equals 1
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integers n, a, b satisfying 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, if r is defined as n - a - b, then the quotient of the q-binomial coefficient of n choose b by the q-binomial coefficient of n choose a equals the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 - q^(r + i)) divided by (1 - q^i), where the q-binomial coefficient is defined using the q-Pochhammer symbols and empty products are 1.

payload.statement_nl: For integers n, a, and b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, define r := n - a - b. Then [n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), where [n choose t]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{n-t}), (q;q)_m := product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j), (q;q)_0 := 1, and an empty product is interpreted as 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Work in the field of fractions of Z[q], so the statement is proved as an identity of rational functions in q. Because 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, we have r = n - a - b >= 0, and hence n - a = b + r and n - b = a + r. In particular, all q-Pochhammer indices appearing below are nonnegative.

By the definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient,
[n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q
= ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})) / ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}))
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{b+r}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{a+r}).

Now let u and v be integers with 0 <= u <= v. From the definition (q;q)_m = prod_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j) and (q;q)_0 = 1, we get
(q;q)_v = (prod_{j=1}^u (1 - q^j)) (prod_{j=u+1}^v (1 - q^j)) = (q;q)_u prod_{j=u+1}^v (1 - q^j),
where the last product is empty and equals 1 when u = v.
Applying this with (u,v) = (a+r, b+r) and with (u,v) = (a, b), we obtain
(q;q)_{b+r} = (q;q)_{a+r} prod_{j=a+r+1}^{b+r} (1 - q^j)
and
(q;q)_b = (q;q)_a prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i).
Substituting these identities into the previous expression gives
[n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{a+r} prod_{j=a+r+1}^{b+r} (1 - q^j)) / (((q;q)_a prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i)) (q;q)_{a+r}))
= (prod_{j=a+r+1}^{b+r} (1 - q^j)) / (prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i)).

Finally, reindex the numerator by j = r + i. As i runs from a+1 to b, j runs from a+r+1 to b+r, so
prod_{j=a+r+1}^{b+r} (1 - q^j) = prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i}).
Therefore
[n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = prod_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^{r+i}) / (1 - q^i)).
If a = b, both products are empty and equal to 1, so the same formula still holds. This is exactly the claimed identity.
result_payload.proof_summary: Expand the two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients, cancel the common factor (q;q)_n, substitute n-a = b+r and n-b = a+r, factor the q-Pochhammer symbols into trailing products, and reindex the numerator product.
